tools.name: check_circuit
tools.description: Checks whether a circuit is wired correctly: loose ends, parts with no power source, an LED with the wrong diode model, unknown parts, labels on top of parts. With "request", also checks that the parts asked for are there (a bulb, an ammeter, a voltmeter, a switch). Checks structure only, not voltag

tools.name: simulate_circuit
tools.description: Simulates a circuit and returns the voltage across and current through every part once it settles, such as the current through an LED, the output of a voltage divider or whether a bulb lights. Also names faults: a short circuit, nothing flowing, an LED over its current rating, a bulb too dim to ligh

tools.name: design_circuit
tools.description: Designs an electronic circuit from a plain description, such as an LED with its resistor, a 555 timer blinker, a transistor switch, a voltage divider, or an Arduino or ESP32 breadboard project with its sketch. The design passes breadboardhub's structural checks, with one corrected attempt if needed;

tools.name: edit_circuit
tools.description: Changes an existing circuit as asked in plain words, such as "make the two resistors parallel", "add a voltmeter across the LED" or "use a 12V supply", or answers a question about it ("what does the 10 mH part do?"). Takes a CircuitJS circuit or a breadboardhub.com/sim link. The changed circuit pass

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Electronics calculators with exact answers: LED resistor value, resistor color code, 555 timer frequency, voltage divider output, Ohm's law, series and parallel resistor totals, RC time constant, RC filter cutoff, transistor base resistor, capacitor code, PCB trace width and battery life. Returns th

tools.name: debug_circuit
tools.description: Finds why a circuit someone built does not work, such as an LED that stays off or a 555 that does not blink on a breadboard. Takes the symptom and either the circuit or a description of what was built, which it draws as built. Simulates that and a proposed fix, and says if the simulator confirms the

tools.name: design_chip
tools.description: Designs digital logic in Verilog from a plain description, such as a 4-bit counter, a traffic light state machine or a logic circuit for an FPGA. Writes the module and a step-by-step test, builds it with Yosys and runs the test on the built circuit, correcting it up to twice. "verified" means it bui

tools.name: fix_chip
tools.description: Fixes Verilog that does not compile or gives warnings, such as syntax errors, width mismatches or unintended latches. Builds it with Yosys and Verilator, corrects it, and builds it again after each change. Returns the corrected code, anything still wrong, and a link that opens it with its diagram. C

tools.name: explain_chip
tools.description: Explains what a Verilog module does, in plain English: its inputs and outputs, its behaviour and anything unusual. Suits learning digital logic or reading FPGA code someone else wrote. Returns the explanation as text; nothing is built or changed. Counts toward the daily design limit.

tools.name: search_designs
tools.description: Searches the public circuit, firmware and schematic designs people have shared on breadboardhub, such as "ESP32 temperature sensor", "buck converter" or "Arduino motor driver". Returns each design's name, type, tags, stars and link. Free, with no daily limit.

tools.name: get_design
tools.description: Gets one public design shared on breadboardhub by its owner's username and its slug, both shown in search results and in design links (breadboardhub.com/<username>/<slug>). Returns its name, type, description, licence, tags, simulator and link. Free, with no daily limit.
